Milton (00:00): Hi everyone. 
 
Joseph Rosslind (00:01): Hi, Milton. How are you? 
 
Milton (00:04): Very, very good. Happy Friday. 
 
Joseph Rosslind (00:06): Happy Friday. Thank you for the new brief. 
 
Milton (00:10): Yeah, of course, of course. I'm really happy to kick up this meeting and kick 
up this campaign with you guys. I'm very excited. But yeah, like we are pretty much ready 
when you, when you're ready, I can definitely just give you some backgrounds and stuff. Are 
you guys ready to go or do you want to add anything before I jump in and start? 
 
Joseph Rosslind (00:30): I'm ready. And I'd like to introduce you to our client service director,

you'd say hi, say hi Jen. 
 
Jen Hird (00:43): I don't even want to sit back, but hi Milton. It's so lovely to meet you. Thank 
you for this brief. 
 
Milton (00:49): Yeah, it's nice to see you. Yes, new brief. I'm very, very, very, very excited and 
our team's really excited to kick up this campaign with you. So yeah, I'll just literally just jump 
in right now. So we've just locked on, we've just locked in our Q3 planning. So the timing is 
pretty good to get this moving. So I've got a fair bit of a run through today. QB has always 
positioned itself as the comprehensive cover insurer. Lots of numbers, lots of policy detail in 
our marketing and we are launching something different today or not today or this time a 
new standalone sub brand called Bellevue Health aimed at reframing Health insurance as 
something that supports people's day to day lives, not just a safety net for when things go 
wrong. 
 
Milton (01:34): So this has come from research last year showing younger members feel 
disconnected from the traditional QBE messaging. They want their cover to feel like a part of 
their everyday routine. Gym sessions, mental Health check ins and that kind of things. And 
to be clear, Bellevue Health is genuinely a new sub brand with its own name and identity. But 
it will be clear it's back by QBE. We are not touching the accor QBE logo or brand identity as 
part of this. Okay, so moving into the objectives and target audiences again, the main 
objective here is the awareness and considering among 25 to 40 years old who don't 
currently have private Health cover or are considering switching providers. The secondary 
objective is making our existing younger members feel more engaged. 
 
Milton (02:23): We've got real churn risk in that segment if that makes sense. And for 
targeting it's mostly metro singles and young couples without kids yet we'll do a separate 
push for families next year. So that's out of scope. For now. And in terms of the deliverables 
channels, there are four deliverables here. So the first one is the Hero video, the 30 seconds 
16 by 9 ratio of course for use on our websites and YouTube. And we'll also need two cut 
 
downs of that same video. A 15 second version and a 6 second bumper, both 9 by 6 in 
vertical for the stories and reels. The next one is the social campaign for meta and 
Instagram. 
 
Milton (03:04): A mix of static and carousel posts which is like a 1080 by 1080 square for the 
feed and 1080 by 1920 for the story. So the vertical one, the next one is the EDM for our 
existing database. Standard single column responsive template header banner at 600 pixel 
wide. We have been using the EDMS a lot with the KB platform, so I'm sure this is not going 
to be a new thing for you guys. The last one is the digital display banner for the retargeting. 
And of course we have those six different standard, standard DV360 file sizes. So that's the 
digital display part that needs to be dispatched as the HTML5 files. And what to add. One 
more thing to make it a bit more complicated for you guys. 
 
Milton (03:58): We want three concept directions to choose from before committing to the full 
production. Of course, I mean if you can come up with the brilliant ideas, that'd be great. And 
we went straight to the one concept last time and then got burned. So this time we need a 
proper options. Any questions so far? 
 
Joseph Rosslind (04:19): Thank you. Milton from QBE for the new brief. I think it is very clear 
and this is one of the most in depth and succinct briefs I've ever received from QBE. And 
that is being truthful. 
 
Milton (04:36): Very good. We have a pretty big budget here as well. The budget for this one 
is 2,300. Oh, sorry, wrong. So the total budget is $980,000 and that needs to cover the 
media spin as well as well as the production. So yeah, and also I'm estimating the 
production is realistically around, you know, 600,000. But I'll leave that one up to you guys 
for you because I know that you guys are going to come up with the cost estimate and 
everything and, and on timing we need to deliver this to be live by the 21st of September. 
 
Milton (05:12): I know this is pretty tight, but we have the Q3 ready to go that time, so we 
definitely need that to be done by 21st September this year and we would like to get the 
initial concepts done by the 31st of July. So we have a bit of room to finalize this. And on the 
amendatories every SM must use the new Bellevue Health lockup logo which our design 
team will send through, plus a small backed by QB endorsement line and the standard 
disclaimer footer which we will be providing in a later stage. And one important thing to flag, I 
only found out this morning. The legal hasn't signed off yet on how we can talk about the 
specific Health claims. Thinking like reduces stress or improves well being might need to be 
softened or removed. 
 
Milton (05:59): I don't have a firm answer on when that will be clear, but for now please treat 
that as an open risk rather than building the whole concept around language that might not 
survive legal review. Yeah, I think that was pretty much it. I know I went through a lot really 
quickly and of course I'll send you the briefs in written briefs. But then yeah, that's pretty 
much it from my end. Do you guys have any questions? 
 
Joseph Rosslind (06:28): No, I thank you again for the succinct new brief. And Jen, did you 
have any questions? 
 
Milton (06:37): Was there something I was supposed to say? 
 
Jen Hird (06:42): No, I don't have any questions. 
 
Milton (06:45): Awesome. Great. Thanks guys. And I'll send you this through to you quickly. 
And I'm assuming you'll be sending me next steps, any questions by the end of next week 
then? 
 
Joseph Rosslind (06:55): So we'll work on a contact report just to report back on that and 
once you respond with that, we can work through timings and what's the requirements. But 
thank you again for the new brief. 
 
Milton (07:06): Awesome. No worries. Thanks guys.
